recipes.name: Garlic Alfredo Tilapia
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon Creole seasoning, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Brush the tilapia fillets with oil on both sides, season with Creole seasoning to taste, then place into a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the flesh is no longer translucent, and the fish flakes easily with a fork, about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the garlic, and cook until the garlic has softened and the aroma has mellowed, about 2 minutes. Stir in the Alfredo sauce and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low, and keep warm until the fish is ready. Pour the sauce over the fish to serve. Sprinkle with additional Creole seasoning if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Alfredo Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: Inspired by the New Orleans seafood dish at a popular restaurant chain, this quick and easy recipe tops tilapia fillets with a garlic-infused Alfredo sauce.

review.reviewBody: This is a simple yet delicious way to serve Tilapia! I had my dinner ready in about 15 minutes...which is amazing for me! I season my fillets with either Penzey's Northwoods Seasoning or Penzey's Jerk seasoning and while it's baking, I make up a quick home-made Alfredo Sauce with 1/4 cup of butter, some fresh garlic, 1/2 cup of half & half, 3/4 cup good Parmesan (grated) and a little Italian seasoning. (Just saute the garlic in the butter over med/high heat, then add the other ingredients, stirring until blended.) This recipe is definitely a keeper - thanks for a new way to serve up Tilapia!

Awesome & easy - the whole family enjoyed this. I made my own creole seasoning (Creole Seasoning Blend recipe from this site). My tilapia from Costco was frozen so it took about 15-min (at 400 in convection) to cook. I also made my own alfredo sauce using the suggestion of another reviewer (1-cup Butter, Fresh Minced Garlic (3/4 of an entire head), 2-tsp Italian Seasoning, 1-tsp Creole Seasoning, 2-cups Dry Parmesan, 1-cup Coffee Cream, 3/4-cup Milk). Served over linguine with steamed broccoli.

Nice change from my regular tilapia recipes. It is very rich so will only make 1 or 2 times a year. Instead of using a jar of Alfredo sauce, I used Quick and Easy Alfredo Sauce by Dawn Carter on this website. We love that sauce & was worth the little extra time it took instead of opening a jar. We made half a recipe for the tilapia. I didn't have enough fresh Parmesan cheese, so had to thicken a little with corn starch & it was still as good as the 5 stars we gave that sauce. Now for the sauce in this recipe being poured over the tilapia, it says use 1 c which I thought was more than really needed for 4 fillets, but that is personal preference.

This was delicious! I made it exactly as the recipe and video describes and I would make the following changes: I would omit the butter and sauté the garlic in a couple of tablespoons of olive oil, then brush the garlic oil over the filets. I would use the creole seasoning more sparingly that shown in the video and I would use less Alfredo sauce and dilute it with some milk or water. The flavors were great together! We had it with a Caesar salad and U can’t wait to make it again!

Living in south Louisiana we eat a lot of fish. I have never used garlic Alfredo on any fish. I made the sauce using 1/3 stick of butter with a little oil, about a tsp of minced garlic, evaporated milk and a handful of shredded Parmesan/Romano blend. I baked Cajun seasoned (one side only) catfish filets in a dish at 450 degrees for about 20 mins until done, then poured the sauce on the fish. This is a great recipe for catfish filets. It’s quick, easy, and there wasn’t a bit of the fish left over. Also good is that it requires only a baking dish and a skillet to prepare. Already looking forward to the next time.

made it as directed. Big crowd pleaser. Made it with a thin Alfredo sauce made with olive oil, flour, chopped sun dried tomato, Parmesan cheese and milk. Broke up the fish and tossed with whole wheat pasta and peas. Easy and delicious.
really good if you add in peppers and onions to the fish and fry it in olive oil with extra creole seasoning. There's a recipe for creole seasoning in this app

Hubby and I Loved it!! I didn’t have any Creole seasoning so I used Bam Bam seasoning ( that is a mix of paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, oregano, basil, thyme, celery and salt.) I also sprinkled lemon juice on the fish before I baked it. I used Asiago cheese Alfredo from a jar and added minced garlic and butter. The fish came out so good! I served it over pasta and broccoli tossed in the Asiago Alfredo sauce with some of the sauce over the fish. I will definitely make this again.

I have a divided household (vegetarian and meat eaters) so I made this with chicken and then tilapia. I prepared the tilapia as noted but also prepared the chicken the same way. I doubled the sauce recipe and added fresh spinach and a can of diced tomatoes with garlic and basil. I served this with penne pasta and it was a hit! I will definitely make this again!

I had a bag of baby spinach I needed to use so I sautéed it and added it to the alfredo sauce. Served it over buttered/peppered spaghetti. My husband and I loved it. So glad I doubled the recipe can't wait to have the leftovers tonight. Thanks for the great recipe!
Fish cooked perfect temp perfect timing. I use garlic alfredo and add cajun season shrimp to the sauce pour over top..delish!

This was pretty good for an easy dinner. Not normally a jarred sauce person but with the added garlic, butter and additional and Cajun seasoning and parm it was okay. I did serve the fish and sauce over mushroom raviolis which hubs seemed to like. Probably will do again because it was so easy.
Tilapia is a very boring fish but this recipe was very good. Easy and quick to make.
We were not fan of too much creole seasoning. Will try again without it. I prepared my own alfredo sauce which I typically use for fettuccine alfredo which I believe is a healthier option.

The baking instructions for the tilapia were perfect, and ones I'll definitely use again. The instructions for the sauce are probably good, but I made one fatal error: I used Garlic Alfredo Sauce and assumed that since it wasn't very strongly flavored, I could just cut the added garlic in half and it would be fine. Now the whole house smells like garlic and the four of us barely touched the sauce. Next time I think I'll make my own *unflavored* alfredo sauce.
I substituted cajun seasoning for the creole seasoning. Really good!
There aren't enough stars to rate this! EASY AND SO GOOD!
Delicious! I subbed step four for making my own alfredo like other reviewers.
So easy to make and so good!!
